Here is a ghost story set in ancient China:

It was the year 1023 CE during the Song Dynasty, and the small village of Xingping was quiet and still under the pale light of the full moon. Most of the villagers were asleep, but one young man named Liang Baoyu was still awake, walking alone through the deserted streets.

Liang worked as a scholar in the local government office, but he often took long nighttime walks to clear his mind. On this particular night, he felt uneasy, as if eyes were watching him from the shadows. The usual comforting sounds of crickets and owls were strangely silent.

As Liang passed the old abandoned temple at the edge of the village, he heard a faint, eerie wailing in the distance. Shivering, he picked up his pace, desperate to get home. But as he neared his house, he saw a pale, ghostly figure standing in the middle of the road. 

The figure was that of a young woman, her long black hair flowing behind her. She turned to face Liang, and he gasped in horror - her face was completely white and sunken, her eyes hollow and lifeless. She opened her mouth and let out a blood-curdling scream that pierced the night air.

Paralyzed with fear, Liang could only stare as the ghostly woman glided towards him. Just before she reached him, he squeezed his eyes shut and a flash of light appeared. When he opened them again, the woman had vanished. All was silent except for the sound of his own shaking breaths.

Liang hurried inside, barring the door behind him. He huddled in the corner, his heart pounding. What dark spirit had he encountered out there in the moonlight? From that night on, Liang never ventured out alone after dark again, haunted by the memory of the vengeful ghost that had nearly claimed him.
